context.exploration_scope: Operationally validated PHASE-SSI-S4's adopted, not-enforced Principle by re-confirming its scope and role differentiation, then applying its own stated logic to one real, current judgment case and comparing against an independently-derived verdict

problem: PHASE-SSI-S4 recorded a Principle as adopted but explicitly not enforced -- it had never actually been applied to a real judgment to see whether the verdict it predicts matches what the existing, already-established decision convention (independent of the new Principle) would produce.

Applied to 1 real judgment case (Is goal_production_runtime actionable right now?): principle_predicted_verdict=DEFERRED, independent_verdict=DEFERRED, match=true. 0 CI wiring, 0 automatic policy, 0 automatic execution, 0 real project modifications. Verdict: PRINCIPLE_OPERATIONALLY_VALIDATED.

action.action_summary: Re-searched the canonical Experience Layer fresh for the Principle grouping, re-verified its scope against the real goal model, re-checked role differentiation against E12s confirmed Pattern registry, then manually applied the Principle to one real judgment case and compared its predicted verdict against an independently-derived verdict from the pre-existing owner_domain convention and a fresh PRODUCTION_VALIDATION_HOLD.json read.

evidence.evidence_detail: principle_predicted_verdict=DEFERRED, independent_verdict=DEFERRED, verdicts_match=true, regression_all_passed=true, dangling=0, duplicates=0

result.note: The Principle, applied by hand to a real current judgment case, produced the same verdict as the independent, already-established owner_domain convention -- operationally validated, still not wired into CI/policy/execution.

cause.root_cause_summary: An adopted-but-unenforced Principle is only a hypothesis about how future judgments should go until it is actually run against one real case and checked against a verdict derived independently of it -- agreement on paper (evidence count, scope, non-conflict) does not by itself prove operational correctness.

lesson: Validating a Principle operationally means applying its own stated logic to a real case and checking the output against a verdict computed by a method that does not itself depend on the Principle -- if both independently-derived paths agree, that is real corroboration; if this phase had instead compared the Principle's prediction only against itself, agreement would have been guaranteed and meaningless.
